researchQuestion: Which compact-object mergers will advanced laser-interferometric gravitational-wave detectors observe first, and with what electromagnetic counterparts?

corpus.title: [SYNTHETIC] Advanced LIGO strain sensitivity projections for compact-binary coalescence searches
corpus.abstract: [SYNTHETIC] Commissioning projections place the advanced-detector strain noise near 1e-23 per root Hz in the 100 Hz band, bringing double neutron-star mergers within reach to hundreds of megaparsecs and heavier black-hole binaries to cosmological distances.

corpus.title: [SYNTHETIC] Short gamma-ray bursts as neutron-star merger electromagnetic signatures
corpus.abstract: [SYNTHETIC] Circumstantial evidence links short gamma-ray bursts to compact-binary coalescence; anticipated r-process heating of merger ejecta should power a days-long red transient detectable by wide-field follow-up.

corpus.title: [SYNTHETIC] Pulsar timing arrays constrain the stochastic gravitational-wave background
corpus.abstract: [SYNTHETIC] Decade-scale pulsar timing residuals bound a nanohertz stochastic background; projected sensitivity improves with array size and cadence.

corpus.title: [SYNTHETIC] Hulse-Taylor binary pulsar orbital decay agrees with quadrupole gravitational-wave emission
corpus.abstract: [SYNTHETIC] Two decades of timing of the binary pulsar PSR B1913+16 track the general-relativistic quadrupole energy loss to within measurement error, establishing indirect evidence of gravitational waves.

targets.statement: Gravitational waves from a binary black-hole merger are directly detected by laser interferometry (GW150914, LIGO and Virgo, Physical Review Letters, 2016).

A binary neutron-star merger is observed in gravitational waves together with an electromagnetic counterpart (kilonova and short gamma-ray burst), founding multi-messenger astrophysics (GW170817, 2017).
targets.unverifiedNote: Multi-paper discovery announced 2017-10-16; the lead multimessenger paper is ApJL 848:L12 but the DOI is not reproduced with high confidence here — verify before citing anywhere.

hypotheses.statement: Coalescing black-hole pairs will provide the first direct gravitational-wave detections in the laser-interferometry band of the advanced detector network.
hypotheses.mechanism: Stellar-origin black-hole binaries radiate chirp signals with amplitudes scaling linearly with total mass, placing their mergers beyond a gigaparsec in the advanced strain band; the heavier and astrophysically plentiful double black-hole channel therefore outranks double neutron-star systems as the first detection source class.

falsificationMethod.prediction: Two years of matched-filter searches over the advanced network report zero binary-black-hole candidates above false-alarm rate 1 per century while double neutron-star candidates accumulate

hypotheses.relationToExistingTheory: Sharpens sensitivity-projection arguments into a ranked prediction of the first source class.
alternativeExplanations: The astrophysical rate of double black-hole mergers is too low for early detection.
observablePredictions: A chirp with tens of solar masses and ringdown consistent with Kerr horizons.
distinguishingObservations: Absence of an electromagnetic counterpart discriminates black-hole from neutron-star mergers.
hypotheses.noveltyRelativeToCorpus: Commits to a detection-ordering claim the corpus stops short of making.
assumptions: Matched-filter pipelines control non-Gaussian detector transients.

hypotheses.statement: A coincident short gamma-ray burst association with any first gravitational-wave event would localize an electromagnetic counterpart within its error region.
hypotheses.mechanism: Wide-field follow-up of a compact-binary coalescence localization scoops the host galaxy; identifying the counterpart pins the distance scale and event rate empirically.

falsificationMethod.prediction: Systematic follow-up campaigns over two observing seasons recover no counterpart candidate within any coalescence localization

hypotheses.relationToExistingTheory: Operationalizes the gamma-ray-burst-merger association into an observing program.
alternativeExplanations: Counterparts are too faint or too slowly evolving for prompt follow-up.
distinguishingObservations: Spectroscopic kilonova-like features versus AGN or supernova interlopers.
hypotheses.noveltyRelativeToCorpus: Program-level claim rather than a new physical mechanism.
assumptions: Localization regions are small enough for wide-field surveys.
risks: Telescope allocation and weather dominate realization odds.

hypotheses.statement: Pulsar timing arrays can constrain a stochastic background from cosmic string networks within a decade.
hypotheses.mechanism: Nanohertz strain from string loops imprints correlated timing residuals across the array; the Hellings-Downs correlation separates it from clock and media noise.

falsificationMethod.prediction: Array sensitivity falls short of the predicted string-background amplitude by an order of magnitude over a decade
